title: Guard attribution for ephemeral delegated API keys and subproject linking
creator: Lena Cho
description:
Summary:
We are seeing a recurring class of multi-tenant attribution errors where short-lived (ephemeral/delegated) API keys used by partner integrations or CI jobs are attributed to the parent org/project instead of the intended subproject or delegated workspace. This manifests after key exchange, subproject linking, or subproject merges and causes billing overcharges on parent accounts plus quota exhaustion on wrong rate-limiter buckets.

Observed behavior & impact:
- Affected events: token-based metering events, rate limiter counters, and quota checks during the token exchange window.
- Customer impact: high — billing spikes for parent orgs, blocked workloads in intended subprojects due to exhausted per-project quotas, and noisy alerts. Several support tickets referenced in the internal billing dashboard (dashboard link below).
- Frequency: intermittent; reproduces reliably when an ephemeral key is created by a service that immediately exchanges for a delegated token and issues requests during a narrow race window (TTL/propagation ~2–7s).

Hypothesis / Root cause (current):
- The attribution pipeline relies on a cached mapping from api_key_id -> project_id maintained in the gateway service and periodically refreshed asynchronously.
- During delegated-key handoffs we create an alias record (parent_api_key -> delegated_token_id) while the canonical mapping update to the new subproject is still propagating. Requests arriving in this window query the cache and fall back to the parent mapping, which causes the billing/quotas system to record usage under the parent project.
- Additional contributor: rate limiter counters are still keyed by "owner_id" derived from the stale cache, so quota exhaustion happens in the wrong bucket instead of the intended subproject.

Repro steps (local/staging):
1) Create parent org and subproject in staging and enable delegated token flow for a service account.
2) Create ephemeral API key A under parent; exchange A for delegated token D (delegation service returns D immediately).
3) Immediately send 50 concurrent generation requests with token D within 0–5s after exchange.
4) Observe that ~10–30% of events are recorded with project_id == parent_project in billing events table and hit the parent's rate limiter counters.

Short-term mitigation (hotfix):
- Block: Add an authoritative check in the ingress path — if an Authorization header contains a delegated-token marker (delegated_token:true) then skip cache fallback and force a synchronous lookup of the canonical key->project mapping (read-through to primary mapping store). This will add ~1–3ms p99 to the edge path but prevents billing misattribution.
- Reconciliation: Trigger a targeted backfill that reattributes events where (token_id in delegated-token-set AND project_id==parent_project) for the affected time range. Backfill pipeline PR linked below.

Long-term fixes / design changes:
- Convert the gateway cache to versioned mappings with prewrite semantics for alias operations so that aliasing (parent->delegate) is only visible after the canonical mapping update has been committed across the fleet.
- Persist token issuance metadata (issuer, delegated_from, intended_project_id) in the canonical token store and require the billing collector to prefer that authoritative field over any cached owner resolution.
- Ensure rate limiter keys are derived from authoritative token metadata rather than cache lookups.

Plan / next steps (this ticket):
- Implement ingress authoritative-check hotfix (rollbackable) and ship to staging for 48h validation. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/1284)
- Run reconciliation pipeline on staging and then prod target window. (Job: https://runbook.internal.redwood/billing/backfill/ephemeral-2026-03)
- Implement unit + integration tests that simulate concurrent delegation and ensure attribution remains correct.
- Begin design work to version cache mappings and add prewrite commit semantics (follow-up epic: billing-epic-attribution-proofs).

Acceptance criteria:
- Hotfix deployed and validated on staging with no regression in p99 latency beyond +5ms baseline; no misattributed events for canonical repro.
- Backfill successfully reapplies correct project_id for all affected tokens in sample window and billing dashboard shows corrected balances for impacted customers.
- End-to-end test coverage added and CI gating for gateway changes.

Artifacts & useful links:
- Billing incident dashboard (redacted): https://dashboards.internal.redwood/billing/ephemeral-attrib-2026-03
- Staging repro script: https://git.internal.redwood/repro/ephemeral-attrib-staging
- Gateway hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/1284
- Backfill PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/542
- Design doc for versioned mappings (draft): https://docs.internal.redwood/confluence/billing/versioned-key-mappings

Owner notes / constraints:
- Be cautious about increasing synchronous reads in the hot path — we expect a small perf hit; product and infra are aware and have signed off for a short mitigation window.
- The backfill must include idempotency checks and cutover verification to avoid double-credits.
